title: GPU-Driven Mesh Generation from Noise Field
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a GPU-driven mesh generation system from a 3D noise field. The scene should demonstrate procedural geometry creation driven by noise parameters with real-time user control.

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x0a0a0f).
- PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 8, 16), looking at origin.
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- One DirectionalLight (white, intensity 1.2) at (5, 10, 7) and one AmbientLight (0x334455, intensity 0.4).
- A subtle grid helper (size 20, divisions 20, color 0x222233) on the XZ plane for spatial reference.

## Noise-Driven Mesh Generation
- Generate a planar mesh grid of configurable resolution (default 64x64 vertices) on the XZ plane, centered at origin, spanning 10x10 units.
- Displace each vertex's Y position using a layered 3D Simplex/Perlin-style noise function (implement a simple hash-based noise in JS — no external noise library). Use 3 octaves of noise with persistence 0.5 and lacunarity 2.0.
- Noise parameters: frequency (default 0.3), amplitude (default 3.0), octaves (default 3), seed (default 42).
- The mesh should use a MeshStandardMaterial with vertexColors enabled. Color each vertex based on its displaced Y height using a gradient: deep blue (y < -1), green (-1 to 0.5), brown (0.5 to 1.5), white (y > 1.5). Compute vertex normals after displacement.
- Support wireframe toggle.

## Animation
- The noise field should animate over time by offsetting the noise sampling coordinates with a time parameter. Animation speed is controllable (default 0.3 units/sec). Animation can be paused/resumed.
- Track elapsed animation time.

## User Interactions
- Key 'R' increments grid resolution through steps: 32, 64, 128, 256. Cycles back to 32. Regenerates the mesh each time.
- Key 'F' cycles noise frequency through: 0.15, 0.3, 0.6, 1.2. Regenerates mesh.
- Key 'A' cycles amplitude through: 1.5, 3.0, 5.0, 8.0. Regenerates mesh.
- Key 'W' toggles wireframe on/off.
- Key 'Space' toggles animation pause/resume.
- Key 'S' changes the noise seed (increment by 1 each press, starting at 42). Regenerates mesh.
- A DOM button with id 'btn-reset' labeled 'Reset All' resets all parameters to defaults (resolution 64, frequency 0.3, amplitude 3.0, seed 42, wireframe off, animation playing, speed 0.3).

## HUD
- A fixed HUD panel (top-left, semi-transparent dark background, white text, monospace font, id='hud') displaying:
  - Resolution: NxN
  - Frequency: value
  - Amplitude: value
  - Octaves: value
  - Seed: value
  - Wireframe: ON/OFF
  - Animation: PLAYING/PAUSED
  - Vertices: count
  - FPS: value (updated each frame)
  - Min Y / Max Y of current mesh displacement

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - resolution (number, current grid resolution e.g. 64)
  - frequency (number)
  - amplitude (number)
  - octaves (number, always 3)
  - seed (number)
  - wireframe (boolean)
  - animationPlaying (boolean)
  - animationTime (number, elapsed time in seconds while playing)
  - vertexCount (number, resolution * resolution)
  - minY (number, minimum Y displacement in current mesh)
  - maxY (number, maximum Y displacement in current mesh)
  - meshExists (boolean, true if terrain mesh is in scene)
  - colorChannelsUsed (boolean, true if geometry has color attribute)
  - normalsComputed (boolean, true if geometry has normal attribute)
  - gridHelperVisible (boolean)
  - fps (number)
  - cameraDistance (number, distance from camera to origin)
  - materialType (string, 'MeshStandardMaterial')
physics_constraints: Vertex displacement must be deterministic for a given seed, frequency, amplitude, and time. The minY and maxY must be bounded by [-amplitude * 2, amplitude * 2] due to octave summation. Vertex count must equal resolution^2. Changing seed with same parameters must produce different terrain. Color mapping must be consistent with Y thresholds.
